title: Devflow review findings
description: What a Devflow reviewer answers about one card's change, and what the review stage keeps as findings.json: one reviewer's report, or several merged with each finding still naming who found it.

card.description: The card id the change belongs to.

base.description: The BASE commit the diff starts from.

previous.description: Set by devpit on a re-review: the earlier run whose HEAD the diff starts from.

mode.description: Set by devpit on a retro review: the range is already merged and in production.

reviewers.description: Who reviewed: one entry for a single reviewer's report, one per reviewer once merged.

verdict.description: request_changes when a finding's severity is in the project's review.block_on (critical and high unless set): the project's rule, which this file cannot see, so it is not checked here. A retro review says follow_up instead: its code is already in production.

done_well.description: What the change does well, specific to it.

pending.description: The personas no reviewer has answered for yet; the review is not complete until it is empty.

dropped.description: Set by devpit: the findings taken out because their line is on no line of HEAD, each with its file, line, axis, title, who found it and the reason.

tests.description: Which tests the reviewer read or ran, and what they prove.

evidence.description: The checks on the card, as the packet reported them.

not_checked.description: What the reviewer could not verify.

agent.description: The agent CLI that ran the review: claude, codex, cursor, gemini.

persona.description: The reviewer persona: devflow-spec, devflow-standards, devflow-security, devflow-all (every axis in one reading), or a project's own.

file.description: Path relative to the repository root.

line.description: Where the problem starts; for something missing, where it belongs.

evidence.description: The quoted line, the rule with its path, or the command and its output.

poc.description: The input, command or request that makes the problem happen. Required, and not empty, for critical and high.

kind.description: What the finding is. missing_test, rule and style are at most medium, and anything in test code short of a defect at most low; a finding without it is read as a defect.

capped.description: Set by devpit when it lowered the severity the reviewer gave: from, the severity said, and why.

found_by.description: Every reviewer that reported this problem, once several reviewers' findings are merged.

agreement.description: How many of the reviewers that looked at this axis found it: 2 of 3.

false_positive.description: The person said it is not a problem; the gate no longer blocks on it.

jev.description: What Jev's devflow-finding rubric said of it — real, severity, duplicate, inside the diff — and, in enforce, what that did: set_aside, a new severity.

carried_from.description: Set by devpit on a re-review: the run this finding, which did not block, was found in. Only the change since was read again, so it still stands.

anchor.description: Set by devpit from the diff and HEAD: the line is one the change added, one a hunk shows around it, outside every hunk of a changed file, or in a file the change did not touch. A finding on no line of HEAD (beyond_eof) is taken out and listed in dropped.

evidence.description: Where the PoC run shows it, or why it was not run.

verified.description: Set by devpit from the session's review.verify step: what running this critical or high's PoC showed. With review.verify: required, a high not confirmed counts as medium and a refuted one holds nothing.

impact.description: A retro review's: the read-only query or log search that shows what this defect touched in production since the deploy. Required of every medium or worse defect there.
